citation.title: Application of Data Assimilation to Transport Simulations of Tokamak Plasmas
citation.authors: Ichikawa, R. E.; Morishita, Y.; Narita, E.; Honda, M.; Urano, H.; Murakami, S.

topic: Ensemble Kalman filter data assimilation of TASK transport simulations using JT-60U Te, ne and Ti profiles
own_question: Whether EnKF data assimilation with an observation model that uses measurement errors improves transport-simulation agreement, and how simple turbulent transport models compare under assimilation.
actual_method_and_evidence: This is an offline retrospective analysis of one NBI-heated JT-60U H-mode shot (44180). It uses six profile time points: the first serves as the initial state and five are assimilated. The method is a 520-member EnKF over the state and diffusivity correction factors. Approach 2 maps state profiles to raw measurement locations through interpolation matrices, with a diagonal observation-noise matrix built from the measurement errors. The paper reports ion-temperature profiles that match observations more closely than TASK without data assimilation, and log-likelihood comparisons across nine model pairs, with CDBM plus the constant model giving the highest value. Hyperparameters were tuned by likelihood on the same shot. There is no held-out data and no real-time demonstration. The Ti source is CXRS, and the text does not specify impurity versus main-ion Ti.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Sequential Bayesian filtering such as the EnKF has been used to combine tokamak profile measurements and their stated errors with a transport model.
claim_checks.qualification: The study is offline, uses one shot, and assimilates only 5 time points. The authors state real-time use as a future aim, not a demonstrated result.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Weighting raw, unevenly spaced observations by their reported errors is a recognized alternative to pre-fitting profiles.
claim_checks.qualification: The improvement is qualitative, for this single shot, and assessed against the same campaign data. It is not shown generally.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are model forecasts updated with profile measurements at sparse times. This is model-state estimation, not causal nowcasting of a pending CES report. Report arrival timing is not addressed.
validation_if_relevant: Validation is in-sample likelihood and visual profile agreement on one shot, with no untouched data.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite it as real-time or 10 ms capable.
Do not cite it as evidence about BES/ECEI or about nowcasting of the CES report.
Do not assert the measured Ti is carbon-impurity Ti.
Do not generalize the CDBM ranking beyond this shot.
Do not imply all prior work is noncausal.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: The paper supports the theoretical background on Bayesian filtering with measurement-error-weighted observation models. It also offers a contrast: physics-model data assimilation versus our data-driven estimation of the current CES report.
